questions.question: Sami asks Mina: 'What is the key to diagnosis in oral medicine?' Mina replies:
options: Careful observation and a methodical approach
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Careful observation and a methodical approach are the keys to diagnosis.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will take the time to observe.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How to differentiate leukoplakia from lichen planus?' Mina replies:
options: Leukoplakia is often unilateral, lichen planus is bilateral and striated
Leukoplakia is bilateral, lichen planus is unilateral
Lichen planus is whiter than leukoplakia
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Lichen planus is bilateral and striated, leukoplakia is often unilateral.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will always check bilaterality.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'When should a leukoplakia be biopsied?' Mina replies:
options: In case of non-homogeneous, verrucous, or sublingual form
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Non-homogeneous, verrucous, or sublingual leukoplakias have a higher risk.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will biopsy at-risk forms.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is the difference between leukoplakia and erythroplakia in terms of risk?' Mina replies:
options: Erythroplakia has a higher risk of malignant transformation
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Erythroplakia has a much higher risk of malignant transformation (up to 90%).' 🦅 Sami: 'I will treat erythroplakias as emergencies.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is verrucous leukoplakia?' Mina replies:
options: A form of leukoplakia with a verrucous surface, at high risk
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Verrucous leukoplakia has a higher risk of malignant transformation.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will biopsy this form.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How to treat erosive lichen planus?' Mina replies:
options: Topical or systemic corticosteroids depending on severity
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Erosive lichen planus often requires corticosteroids.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will refer to a specialist.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What are the signs of severity of lichen planus?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Erosive, atrophic, or bullous forms are more severe.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will monitor these forms.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is contact stomatitis?' Mina replies:
options: An inflammatory reaction to a local allergen (toothpaste, food, material)
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Contact stomatitis is a reaction to an allergen.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will question the patient about their habits.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'How to diagnose oral candidiasis?' Mina replies:
options: Clinical appearance (white patches) and direct examination or culture
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Diagnosis is clinical, sometimes confirmed by direct examination.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will recognize the clinical appearance.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What are the risk factors for oral candidiasis?' Mina replies:
options: Antibiotic therapy, corticosteroid therapy, immunosuppression, diabetes, xerostomia
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The risk factors are multiple.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will look for these factors.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'How is oral candidiasis treated?' Mina replies:
options: Topical antifungals (nystatin, miconazole) or systemic if severe
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Treatment is antifungal.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will prescribe nystatin.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is atrophic glossitis?' Mina replies:
options: An inflammation of the tongue with atrophy of the papillae, often linked to deficiency
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Atrophic glossitis is often linked to deficiencies.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will request a blood test.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What are the causes of atrophic glossitis?' Mina replies:
options: Iron deficiency, vitamin B12, folic acid
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Nutritional deficiencies are the main causes.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will prescribe a deficiency workup.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is geographic tongue?' Mina replies:
options: A benign condition of the tongue with depapillated areas and raised borders
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Geographic tongue is a benign condition.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will reassure the patient.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is burning mouth syndrome?' Mina replies:
options: A burning sensation without clinical lesion, often in menopausal women
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'It's a complex syndrome, often in menopausal women.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will look for associated factors.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How is burning mouth syndrome treated?' Mina replies:
options: Treatment of underlying causes, analgesics, anxiolytics if necessary
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Treatment is symptomatic and etiological.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will look for the cause.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is angular cheilitis?' Mina replies:
options: An inflammation of the lip commissures, often due to Candida or deficiency
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Angular cheilitis is often due to Candida and deficiencies.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will treat the cause.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How is angular cheilitis treated?' Mina replies:
options: Topical antifungal, correction of deficiencies, hydration
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Treatment is multifactorial.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will prescribe an antifungal and vitamins.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is nicotinic stomatitis?' Mina replies:
options: Palatal keratosis due to tobacco, often benign
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'It's a benign lesion related to tobacco.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will advise smoking cessation.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What are the warning signs in oral medicine?' Mina replies:
options: Persistent lesion > 3 weeks, induration, bleeding, ulceration, pain
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'These signs should raise an alarm.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will always look for these signs.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'When should a biopsy be performed in oral medicine?' Mina replies:
options: Before any persistent lesion > 3 weeks or suspicious lesion
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Biopsy is indicated for a persistent or suspicious lesion.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will biopsy persistent lesions.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What are the risk factors for oral cavity cancer?' Mina replies:
options: Tobacco, alcohol, HPV, sun exposure, age
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The risk factors are numerous.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will inform my patients of the risks.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What are the prevention measures for oral cancer?' Mina replies:
options: Smoking and alcohol cessation, HPV vaccination, sun protection, self-examination
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Prevention is multifactorial.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will raise awareness among my patients.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is an oral biopsy?' Mina replies:
options: A tissue sample for histopathological analysis
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Biopsy is a tissue sample.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will learn how to do biopsies.'

questions.question: Sami, after mastering diagnosis with Mina, says: 'I am ready to take on any challenge!' Mina concludes: 'Mastering diagnosis in oral medicine is...'
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Mastering diagnosis in oral medicine is the basis of management.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will continue to improve.'
